criteria.name: Hook strength
criteria.notes: Opens by naming Berkowitz and Far North Digital, quotes the claim, and signals a corrective with 'the half it gets wrong changes the price tag' — concrete and snark-free. Narrowly misses 10 because the company name front-runs the claim itself.

criteria.name: Claim load-bearing + AK stakes
criteria.notes: Claim directly drives Far North Digital's capital raise framing, investor pricing, governor's 2031 timeline, and Microsoft/Google/Amazon hyperscaler evaluation. Both the claim and the AK consequence (financing structure, BEAD funding, trans-Pacific build cost) are substantive and specific.

criteria.name: Steelman fairness
criteria.notes: Paragraph 3 grants rural Alaska broadband is genuinely thin, the lower-48 link has outage history, and the trans-Pacific gap is real — consistent with the dossier steelman. A claim believer feels fairly represented. No snark.

criteria.name: Counter-evidence quality
criteria.notes: Three rebuttal points each trace to dossier counter_evidence: ACEP UAF blog (primary), Dunleavy/Data Center Knowledge (primary official statement), Alaska Communications $124.5M BEAD grant via Homer News (primary). All marked is_primary true in the dossier.

criteria.name: Factual density
criteria.notes: Named facts appear nearly every 1-2 sentences: Berkowitz, Far North Digital, UAF/ACEP, Dunleavy, Data Center World, 12ms latency, March 2026, $124.5M, NTIA BEAD, seven named cities, 2019 fiber, 2031 timeline, Microsoft/Google/Amazon. Connective paragraph is the only slightly thinner moment.

criteria.name: Source quality
criteria.notes: Claim attributed to a named, dated ADN op-ed (primary). Counter-evidence sources are ACEP UAF blog, Data Center Knowledge, and Homer News, all primary and in dossier. Homer News is a local paper rather than a federal docket, keeping this just off 10, but all are credible and independently originated.

criteria.name: Voice match
criteria.notes: Analytical, structural, business-literate, corrective without contempt. 'Here's where it breaks' and 'the accurate frame is narrower and more investable' are confident position-taking. No influencer cadence or hype. Minor: 'more investable' edges slightly toward pitch language.

criteria.name: Readability (LinkedIn)
criteria.notes: Paragraphs are tight (2-4 sentences), 429 words in range, 2715 chars under cap. Single bullet block has only one item where the descriptor calls for 3-5 single-clause items, a minor structural deviation.

criteria.name: Engagement question
criteria.notes: Closing question is real, debatable, tied directly to the corrected frame, and forces a genuine strategic choice. No softeners, no CTA.

criteria.name: Business actionability
criteria.notes: An allocator or program manager can leave with a concrete reframe: price a single trans-Pacific link, not a statewide rebuild, against the 2031 timeline and hyperscaler evaluation.

one_sentence_fix: Expand the single-item bullet block to 3-5 distinct single-clause items enumerating the specific gaps (trans-Pacific route, Asia-Pacific latency, rural last-mile) so the structure matches the rubric's scannability target.
